subtopics.title: South Africa's Energy Mix: Thermal and Hydro

questions.question: Giant thermal stations like Kendal, Majuba, Medupi and Kusile cluster on the Mpumalanga and Waterberg coalfields because:
options: It is far cheaper to send electricity down a wire than to rail coal across the country
The coalfields have the coolest climate for machinery
Gauteng refused to host power stations
Water is most abundant there

questions.question: South Africa's hydro-electric contribution is small because:
options: Turbine technology is unavailable locally
The country is dry with variable rivers — the water constraint limits true hydro to stations like Gariep and Vanderkloof plus imports from Cahora Bassa
Hydro-electricity cannot supply peaks
All rivers flow away from the escarpment

questions.question: Pumped storage schemes like Drakensberg, Palmiet and Ingula are best described as:
options: True hydro-electric sources adding net energy
Backup diesel systems
Giant batteries — pumping water uphill with cheap off-peak power and releasing it through turbines at peak, consuming more energy than they produce
Desalination plants with turbines

questions.question: South Africa's electricity mix is approximately:
options: Half coal, half hydro
Mostly nuclear with a coal sliver
Evenly split among coal, nuclear and renewables
Roughly 80 per cent coal, with slivers for nuclear (Koeberg), hydro, pumped storage and growing renewables

questions.question: The energy chain in a coal station runs:
options: Chemical energy to heat to kinetic energy to electrical energy — coal, steam, spin, spark
Electrical to kinetic to heat to chemical
Heat to chemical to electrical to kinetic
Kinetic to heat to chemical to electrical

questions.question: Coal is pulverised to flour-fine powder before burning because:
options: Powder is easier to transport by rail
Powder burns fast and completely in the furnace
It reduces the ash produced to zero
Whole coal cannot ignite

questions.question: Transmission uses voltages stepped up to as much as 400 kilovolts because:
options: Generators naturally produce that voltage
High voltage is safer for households
High voltage cuts energy losses over long distances, with substations stepping it down near users
Transformers cannot reduce voltage

questions.question: Dry-cooled stations like Kendal and Matimba are a South African speciality because:
options: They burn less coal per unit
They need no turbines
Dry cooling produces extra electricity
They were designed for water-scarce sites, using air instead of the water that wet-cooled towers consume

questions.question: Baseload power matters because:
options: It is steady power delivered day and night, wind or still — what keeps hospitals, smelters and traffic lights alive
It is the cheapest kind of solar power
It only operates during peak hours
It requires no fuel

questions.question: Acid mine drainage is a long-lived cost of coal because:
options: Power station ash acidifies rain clouds
Water turned acidic and metal-laden in old workings seeps from abandoned mines toward rivers, a bill outliving the mine by a century
Acid is used to wash coal before burning
It only occurs while mines are operating

questions.question: Emalahleni appears on both sides of the coal ledger because:
options: It hosts both coal mines and wind farms
Its name means place of gold
Coal wages support the town while the polluted Highveld airshed damages its residents' health
It exports coal but imports electricity

questions.question: Load-shedding demonstrated that:
options: South Africa ran out of coal reserves
Electricity demand fell too low
Renewables caused grid instability
Even abundant coal fails without functioning machines — the ageing, under-maintained fleet was the weak link

subtopics.title: Can Conventional Sources Carry the Future? Nuclear as Case Study

questions.question: Koeberg's essential facts are:
options: Two reactors of about 1 900 megawatts near Cape Town, supplying Western Cape baseload since 1984 — Africa's only nuclear power station
A coal station converted to nuclear in 2000
Four reactors on the Mpumalanga coalfields
A research reactor that supplies no grid power

questions.question: The concentration of nuclear fuel is captured by:
options: One tonne of uranium equalling one tonne of coal
A fingertip-sized uranium pellet holding the energy of about a tonne of coal
Uranium burning hotter than coal in the same furnace
Nuclear stations needing no turbines

questions.question: Nuclear's main disadvantages include:
options: Carbon emissions during operation and ash disposal
Dependence on imported fuel only
The highest construction costs and longest build times in the energy world, waste needing isolation for thousands of years, and rare but enormous accident risk
Inability to supply baseload

questions.question: The lesson's conclusion on conventional-only supply is:
options: Coal alone can carry the century
Nuclear alone should replace coal immediately
Hydro can be expanded to dominate the mix
Conventional sources alone cannot carry long-term needs — coal's constraints are structural and nuclear is slow and costly — so the realistic path is a mix

subtopics.title: The Kettle the Size of a Suburb

questions.question: In the kettle picture, the generator is:
options: A spinning magnet inside coils of wire — motion becoming electricity
The furnace that burns the coal
The cooling tower
The transformer at the gate

questions.question: The white clouds above the funnel-shaped towers are:
options: Smoke from burning coal
Water vapour from cooling the used steam — the actual smoke leaves by the tall thin stacks
Ash being dispersed
Steam leaking from the turbines

questions.question: 'Send the electricity travelling, not the coal' explains:
options: Why coal exports go through Richards Bay
Why transformers step voltage down
Why stations huddle on the coalfields while high-voltage lines carry power to distant Gauteng
Why stations are built near cities

questions.question: 'One truck in three' refers to:
options: The share of coal lost in transport
The portion of trucks carrying ash
Coal reserves lasting three more decades
Only about a third of coal's chemical energy leaving as electricity — the rest is heat lost to the sky

questions.question: The receipts drawer for coal contains:
options: Historically cheap power that built industry, steady baseload, about ninety thousand mining jobs, coal towns and Richards Bay exports
Only the profits of Eskom
Carbon taxes already paid
Water savings from wet cooling

questions.question: The 'nastiest line item' in the bills drawer is:
options: The cost of conveyor belts
Acid mine drainage — old flooded mines leaking acidic, metal-heavy water toward rivers a century after closing
Rising train fares
The price of turbine blades

questions.question: The land bill of coal includes:
options: Urban sprawl around Johannesburg
Soil salinisation from irrigation
Opencast pits consuming the same Mpumalanga farmland that grows much of the maize crop
Overgrazing near power stations

questions.question: 'Coal built the house AND is quietly burning some of it down' is the reminder that:
options: Coal stations frequently catch fire
The house always wins
Coal's era ended in the 1990s
Any honest answer opens both drawers — real benefits and real, accumulating costs together

questions.question: The road signs that turn coal-only into a countdown include:
options: An ageing fleet, banks refusing new coal finance, looming carbon border taxes, water constraints and climate commitments
Empty coal reserves by 2030
A ban on electricity exports
The closure of Richards Bay terminal

questions.question: From the steam onward, a nuclear station is 'just the kettle again' because:
options: Nuclear stations boil water at lower temperatures
Fission heat raises steam that drives a turbine and generator exactly as in any thermal plant
Uranium is burned in the same furnace as coal
Nuclear stations have no cooling systems

questions.question: South Africa's nuclear waste is stored:
options: At sea beyond the continental shelf
Beneath the Mpumalanga coalfields
At Koeberg and at the Vaalputs facility in the Northern Cape
It is exported for reprocessing

questions.question: The exam-safe verdict at the fork is:
options: Choose coal until the reserves run out
Choose nuclear exclusively despite the cost
Choose imported electricity
No single source can carry the future — coal is counting down, nuclear is clean but slow and dear — so the answer is a mix
